narrative.h2: From audio file to finished music video in one pass

sections.heading: What 'maker' means versus 'editor'
sections.body: An AI music video maker is the one-shot tool — you give it a song, it gives you back a finished video. No timeline, no clip-by-clip prompting, no manual asset wrangling. The trade-off is control: makers optimize for getting something watchable in the first three minutes, not for the surgical edit pass an editor enables. For drafts, demos sent to a label, or 'does this song even need a video?' tests, that's exactly the right tool.

sections.heading: What Tunee's maker actually decides for you
sections.body: Drop an MP3 and Tunee picks the aesthetic from the audio itself: a lo-fi beat lands in muted color and slow camera drifts, a drill instrumental gets high-contrast night exteriors and faster cuts, a worship piano ballad goes lyric-forward with warm key light. You can override the style with one line of prompt, but the default is rarely embarrassing — which is the actual bar most 'AI MV maker' tools fail to clear.

sections.heading: The agent chain that makes the call
sections.body: Four agents run in sequence: the audio analyst extracts tempo, key, and emotional arc; Nova drafts the visual world (characters, palette, environment); Sage cuts those plates into a timed shot list mapped to the song's structure; the renderer produces final frames. The maker route runs all four with smart defaults — the editor route exposes the same chain so you can intervene at any step. Same engine, different surface.
